Simple Past Passive to Report Events
You can use the passive voice when you want to report events that happened in the past in a general way.

Most of spoken English uses active speech. When you use an active sentence to report an event, the subject is the focus of the sentence.
Example:
  • Extreme Sports Africa (subject) organized this centenarian's jump (object).

A passive sentence puts the emphasis on the object of the active sentence. When you use a passive sentence to report an event, the object of the active sentence now becomes the subject and focus of the passive sentence.
Example:
  • This centenarian's jump (subject) was organized by Extreme Sports Africa (object).

You can use the Simple Past passive form to report events in an impersonal way. The subject is not specific, but general.
Example:
  • It was reported that Marion Van Loon became the first person over 100 to parachute out of a plane.
You make the passive form of a verb by using tenses of the be verb followed by the past participle.
Firstly, her stamina and strength was increased by using a conditioning coach.
During the jump, Oxygen masks were worn by Marian and her instructor.
The previous record of William Johansson, an 89 year old veteran from Colorado, was shattered by this jump once Marion landed.
This centenarian's jump was organized by Extreme Sports Africa and funding was provided by donations.
Passive of Modal Verbs in the Past
You use the Simple Past passive form of Modal verbs to put the emphasis on the receiver of the action.

As for other verbs, the Simple Past passive form of modal verbs puts the emphasis on the receiver of the action and not on the doer of the action.
Passive modal forms are often impersonal and do not require an object.
Example:
  • Sports shoes must be worn on the field.
  • Baseball may be played on Tuesdays.
The structure of Simple Past passive for modal verbs is:
subject+modal verb+have been+past participle of verb  </br></br>You can use Simple Past modal verbs to convey certainty, possibility, or uncertainty about a past event or situation.

Centenarian Soars In Kilimanjaro

Turning 100 should have been considered remarkable for Marion Van Loon. However, this dedicated skydiver took a leap of faith on June 19th when she became the first person over 100 years old to parachute out of a plane above the clouded peaks of Africa's highest mountain.
Marion Van Loon, from Norway, had to spend months preparing for the event. Firstly, her stamina and strength was increased by using a conditioning coach. Training included long walks with her grandchildren and weekly visits to the pool.

There were initial fears that the jump could have been delayed because of unpredictable weather but improved during the night.
The parachutist's plane must have flown only about 200 meters above the majestic mountain at sunrise when the doors were opened.
</br>
During the jump, oxygen masks were worn by Marian and her instructor. Otherwise, the air might have been too thin for them to breathe safely.  They were in free fall for 35 seconds before their chutes opened. At that point, Marion was awestruck by the scenery as she glided towards the landing zone. A member of Van Loon's family explained to the crowd. “Granny is an inspiring woman, “ she said. The previous record of William Johansson, an 89-year-old veteran from Colorado, was shattered by this jump once Marion landed.

Marion was ecstatic with her jump. She exclaimed: "My amazing jump should encourage older citizens to be more active. Don't be a couch potato. Get off the couch and get moving!" Being active runs in Marion's  family. Her 80 year old son recently competed in the Masters Games as a sprinter while her granddaughter runs half-marathons. If you are a thrill seeker, itineraries such as this one can be organized by a number of agencies. The centenarian's jump was organized by Extreme Sports Africa and funding was provided by donations.
